source: Shared Miniature Festival World — Technical Spec v3.0, §6 (8 Loops) + §1 roadmap

epics.summary: Loop 0 — Dev Workflow & Loop Engineering Setup
epics.description: Tooling that lets Claude run Spec → Prompt → Code → Test → Refine per ticket: spec as markdown, project CLAUDE.md, agents, loop skills, CI and a merge gate.

stories.summary: Convert spec v3.0 PDF to docs/spec markdown
stories.goal: Agents read the spec as diff-able markdown instead of a PDF.
ac: docs/spec/00-scope.md … 05-privacy-db.md and docs/spec/06-loops/loop-1.md … loop-8.md exist
Every section, formula and table of the PDF is present (coordinate formulas, DB columns, task lists)
Thai text is preserved verbatim; no content invented

stories.summary: Project CLAUDE.md + project agents (privacy-auditor, r3f-perf-reviewer)
stories.goal: Every agent knows the invariants it must not break.
ac: CLAUDE.md lists invariants: parametric coords only, 3D/2D share one coord set, public payload never contains owner_token/owner_token_hash/private_wish_text, zone ≤ 80–100 items, object pools, dispose on zone switch
CLAUDE.md lists standard commands (typecheck, lint, test, build, e2e) and branch/commit conventions with MFW keys
.claude/agents/privacy-auditor.md and r3f-perf-reviewer.md exist, read-only tools

stories.summary: Loop skills: spec-to-jira, loop-ticket, loop-epic
stories.goal: One command runs a ticket (or a whole epic) end-to-end: Jira → branch → lead/dev/reviewer∥qa → PR → merge → Jira Done.
ac: loop-ticket picks the next unblocked To Do ticket, transitions it, branches feat/MFW-<n>-<slug>, runs the full agent loop, opens a PR
Merges only after CI is green and reviewer/qa pass; otherwise labels needs-human, comments the reason and stops
spec-to-jira is idempotent (matches on spec:task-x.y label)
loop-epic runs loop-ticket over one epic in dependency order and writes an epic report

stories.summary: CI pipeline + skill-enforced merge gate
stories.goal: Nothing reaches main without typecheck, lint, unit tests, build and a smoke e2e passing.
ac: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs pnpm install → typecheck → lint → vitest → build → playwright smoke (WebGL via SwiftShader + FALLBACK_2D mode)
Because GitHub Free has no branch protection on private repos, loop-ticket waits for `gh pr checks` green before merging
Vercel preview URL is posted on the PR; previews do not need Supabase env

stories.summary: Cloud-ready loop: in-repo agents, REST GitHub mode, proxy Jira auth
stories.goal: /loop-ticket and /loop-epic run unattended in a fresh Claude Code cloud session (no ~/.claude files, no GitHub GraphQL, Jira auth injected by the network proxy).
ac: lead, dev, reviewer and qa agents live in .claude/agents/ with their models (lead opus; dev, reviewer, qa sonnet); loop-ticket no longer depends on any file under ~/.claude

GitHub steps (open PR, wait for the ci check on the exact head SHA, squash merge pinned to that SHA) work through the GitHub REST API only; cloud mode uses no `gh auth token -u` and no GraphQL-only gh commands
scripts/jira.mjs works with credentials injected by the network proxy (no jira.env file) and routes its HTTPS calls through HTTPS_PROXY by itself
playwright.config.ts uses PW_CHROMIUM_PATH and E2E_PORT when set; defaults are unchanged
loop-epic can run independent ready tickets in parallel git worktrees, merges them one at a time (rebase + green ci before each merge) and stops at a per-run ticket cap
Tickets labelled privacy, db or migration get a PR but are never auto-merged; they wait for the owner
docs/cloud.md documents the environment setup and the daily unattended run

epics.summary: Loop 1 — Project Foundation, Config Schema & Adaptive Performance Engine
epics.description: Spec §6.1. Core project, flow state machine, unified coordinate converters, device profiler & quality tiers.

stories.summary: Setup core project & flow state machine
stories.goal: Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind + Zustand app with the user-flow state machine and event selector.
ac: Flow state machine: LANDING_EVENT_SELECT → CUSTOMIZE_OBJECT → WRITE_WISH → RITUAL_RELEASE → SHARED_WORLD_EXPLORE with unit tests for every transition
Event selector enables Loy Krathong; other roadmap festivals show Coming Soon via feature flag
Folder structure follows spec §3 (config/events, core/*, components/*, services/*, store/*)
Zustand stores split: UI, Customization (useBuilderStore), World (useWorldStore), Device (useDeviceStore)

stories.summary: Unified coordinate converter module
stories.goal: Parametric coords convert losslessly between DB ↔ 3D world ↔ 2D canvas.
ac: SplinePathCoord implemented: CurrentProgress(t) = (spawnProgress + (now − createdAt) × speedFactor) % 1.0; 3D via CatmullRomCurve3 + lateralOffset perpendicular to flow
Interfaces (typed) for NormalizedCylindricalCoord and PlanarZoneCoord
Round-trip unit tests: Parametric ↔ 3D world position ↔ 2D canvas position within tolerance
No raw (x,y,z) is ever persisted

stories.summary: Mobile hardware profiler & quality tier switcher
stories.goal: The app picks HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW automatically and falls back to 2D when needed.
ac: FPS meter + device capability detection + prefers-reduced-motion
Auto tier HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW, switches to FALLBACK_2D when WebGL is unavailable or FPS stays below threshold
State lives in useDeviceStore (fps, qualityTier, reducedMotion, isFallback2D); thresholds in performance.config.ts

epics.summary: Loop 2 — Privacy, Security & Anonymous Ownership Vault
epics.description: Spec §5 + §6.2. Anonymous ownership token, public/private table split, PII guard, profanity filter, report endpoint.

stories.summary: Client-side anonymous ownership token (DeviceOwnerToken)
stories.goal: Users own their creations without accounts.
ac: Cryptographically secure random token stored in LocalStorage; the server stores only its SHA-256 hash (the raw token goes only over HTTPS to the ownership endpoints and is never stored or logged — open question 1)
UI warns that clearing browser data or changing device loses access to own creations
Unit tests for generation, persistence, hashing

stories.summary: Public/private separated API & database
stories.goal: Public data and ownership data never mix in any public payload.
ac: Supabase tables creations_public (id, event_id, zone_id, appearance JSONB, coord JSONB, public_wish_text, created_at, expires_at) and creations_private_ownership (creation_id FK, owner_token_hash, private_wish_text encrypted, report_count, moderation_status enum)
RLS on both; creations_private_ownership is not exposed to the anon Data API
GET /api/creations?event=loy_krathong&zone=1 returns only public fields; test asserts owner_token / owner_token_hash / private_wish_text never appear
Zone pagination: ≤ 80 items per zone (owner decision, open question 4)

stories.summary: PII guard, profanity filter & report endpoint
stories.goal: Public wishes cannot leak personal data or abuse.
ac: Detects phone numbers, emails, LINE IDs, social handles and banned words before save (rules in moderation.config.ts); Thai + English test cases
User is warned and blocked from publishing PII publicly
Report button endpoint increments report_count and flags/hides per threshold

stories.summary: Create-creation API (server write path)
stories.goal: One server endpoint owns every write of a creation, so hashing, encryption, moderation and coordinate validation cannot be skipped.
ac: POST /api/creations takes eventId, appearance, coord, wishText, wishVisibility (private | public) and ownerToken in the JSON body; coord must pass parsePersistableCoord and appearance the event's appearance validator; unknown fields are rejected
The server stores only SHA-256(ownerToken) in creations_private_ownership; the raw token is never stored, logged or returned

A private wish is stored only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext with a key id (public_wish_text stays null); a public wish must pass the 2.3 guard on the server (rejected with the reasons otherwise) and private_wish_text stays null
The server assigns zone_id (first zone of the event below the 80-item cap, else a new zone) and expires_at (festival end + 30 days, from config); the client cannot set them
The response contains only public fields; a test asserts owner_token, owner_token_hash and private_wish_text never appear; the route works with an in-memory repository when Supabase env is absent

No overlap (open question 25): the server re-checks the coord against the krathongs already in the zone and moves it to the nearest free spot (collision radius from config) when two releases race; the response returns the final coord

epics.summary: Loop 3 — Minimal Toy-like 3D Viewport & Mobile Input Separation
epics.description: Spec §6.3. Toy-like night river look, input modes that separate camera vs placement, camera fly-to & highlight.

stories.summary: Toy-like 3D LookDev (night river ambience)
stories.goal: The miniature-world look the rest of the scene builds on.
ac: Orthographic camera, soft night lighting, warm candle light
Matte, slightly rounded, non-glossy materials
Respects quality tier from useDeviceStore

stories.summary: Input separator — camera vs placement on mobile
stories.goal: No accidental drags or taps on mobile.
ac: CUSTOMIZE: drag rotates the krathong, pinch zooms
RITUAL_RELEASE: camera locked at the pier; drag krathong into water, or a Release button for users who can't gesture
WORLD_EXPLORE: drag pans/rotates the river; short tap interacts with water, lamps, krathongs
Tests cover mode switching

stories.summary: Camera fly-to & highlight controller
stories.goal: Smoothly bring any object into clear view.
ac: flyTo(target) eases camera to a target position and a clear viewing angle
Highlight ring effect around the target, follows a moving target
Reduced-motion users get an instant cut instead of an animated flight

stories.summary: Loop 3 retro-review fixes: lazy 3D scene, interactive-mode canvas, ritual camera lock
stories.goal: Fix the findings of the retro review of MFW-15/16/17 (merged without the loop's review gate) that do not belong to a later ticket.
ac: The 3D scene code (three, @react-three/fiber, @react-spring/three) is loaded lazily and only after the device profiler has decided a tier other than FALLBACK_2D: the landing page's initial JS contains no WebGLRenderer chunk, and FALLBACK_2D never downloads it

The scene canvas is mounted only in the modes that use it (CUSTOMIZE_OBJECT, RITUAL_RELEASE, SHARED_WORLD_EXPLORE); LANDING and WRITE_WISH render no canvas and no touch-none block, so page scroll is never trapped
RITUAL_RELEASE keeps the camera locked: a tap on water or an object never triggers flyTo or a highlight; selection and highlight are cleared on every mode change
The camera options passed to the canvas are a stable object across renders (pinch zoom survives drag re-renders), covered by a test
e2e: a canvas exists on a 3D tier and none exists on FALLBACK_2D (stubbed tier/WebGL); component tests drive the pointer flow with a real or stub R3F context instead of a mocked Canvas

epics.summary: Loop 4 — Loy Krathong Modular Customization & Wish Composer
epics.description: Spec §6.4. Modular krathong assembler with socket rules, mobile-first customizer UI, wish composer modal.

stories.summary: Krathong modular assembler & socket rules
stories.goal: Build a krathong from shared parts with enforced placement rules.
ac: Parts: base (banana trunk / lotus petal / toy bread), bananaLeaves fold styles & colors, flowers (marigold, orchid, lotus) on rim sockets, candleAndIncense
candleAndIncense constrained to center_socket and always upright on the Y axis
Parts share geometry/material; appearance serializes to the appearance JSONB shape in spec §5
Unit tests for socket validator

stories.summary: Mobile-first customizer UI (CustomizerPanel)
stories.goal: Pick parts and colors comfortably with one thumb.
ac: Bottom bar for parts and colors; rotate-around and zoom-detail controls
Gentle bounce animation on part change (off under reduced motion)
Works at 360px width

stories.summary: Wish / let-go composer modal (WishModal)
stories.goal: Write a wish and choose clearly between private and anonymous public.
ac: Explicit choice: keep private vs publish anonymously
PII warning and blocking via the 2.3 guard before publishing
Private text goes only to private_wish_text; public text only to public_wish_text

epics.summary: Loop 5 — Loy Krathong Ritual, River Spline Movement & Growing River Zones
epics.description: Spec §6.5. Make & Release ritual, deterministic spline flow, growing river zones with pagination.

stories.summary: "Make & Release" ritual interaction
stories.goal: The emotional core: releasing your krathong onto the river.
ac: Pier scene previews the user's own krathong before release
Drag into water or press "ปล่อยกระทง" → ripple, candle brightens, krathong drifts out into the shared river
Creation is saved with a SplinePathCoord

Releasing onto another krathong collides instead of overlapping (open question 25): a short procedural bump plays (instant under reduced motion) and the new krathong settles in the nearest free spot, which is the coord that is saved

stories.summary: Deterministic spline river flow
stories.goal: Every client sees every krathong at the same place at the same time.
ac: River lanes as spline curves (one single wide lane, open question 21); krathongs move slowly with procedural bobbing (bobbing off under reduced motion, drift continues — open question 23)
Every krathong drifts at the same speed, so krathongs never overlap while drifting (open question 25); at the lane end a krathong reappears at the start off-screen (open question 22)
Position computed only from SplinePathCoord + current time (deterministic across clients and 2D/3D)
Current position queryable for Find My Krathong

stories.summary: Growing river world & zone pagination
stories.goal: The world grows instead of overcrowding one scene.
ac: Max 80 krathongs rendered per river-bend zone (owner decision, open question 4)
New zones (Zone 2, 3, …) open along the river as participation grows (ZoneManager / GrowingWorldScaler)
Only the visible zone is loaded

epics.summary: Loop 6 — Loy Krathong Scene Environment & Interactive Gimmicks
epics.description: Spec §6.6. Low-poly night river environment and tap gimmicks with object pooling.

stories.summary: Low-poly night river environment
stories.goal: Charming but cheap scenery that keeps krathongs the focal point.
ac: Riverside wooden houses, trees, riverside lamps, pier
Low detail; interactive krathongs remain the most visually prominent objects
Fits the quality-tier budgets

stories.summary: Interactive scene gimmicks & object pool
stories.goal: Small delights on tap without frame drops.
ac: Tap water → stylized ripple, concurrent ripples capped by ObjectPoolManager
Tap lamp → warm light up/flicker with small bounce
Tap a krathong → gentle bounce + InspectPopup with appearance and anonymous public wish + Report button

epics.summary: Loop 7 — Find My Krathong & Cross-Zone Tracking
epics.description: Spec §6.7. My Creations drawer, real-time tracking across zones, owner private view.

stories.summary: My Creations drawer & real-time position tracker
stories.goal: "ค้นหาของฉัน" finds your moving krathong anywhere on the river.
ac: Drawer lists krathongs created on this device (via DeviceOwnerToken)
Selecting one: await loadZone(zoneId) if in another zone → compute current position from SplinePathCoord → flyTo + highlight that follows it
Works when the krathong is in a different zone from the current view

stories.summary: Anonymous wish reader & owner private view
stories.goal: Others see only public text; owners can read their own private text.
ac: Other users' krathongs show only public text, no name or profile
Own krathong (verified by presenting the DeviceOwnerToken, compared server-side with its stored SHA-256 hash) can reveal its private wish
Test: private text is never returned without a matching owner token

epics.summary: Loop 8 — Flat Vector 2D Fallback & Mobile Performance Polish
epics.description: Spec §6.8. Full 2D fallback on the same coordinates, instancing and memory cleanup.

stories.summary: Flat vector 2D fallback renderer
stories.goal: Devices without good 3D still get the full experience.
ac: Layered 2D flat-vector krathong customizer
Semi top-down 2D river reading the same SplinePathCoord; 2D ripples on tap; Find My Krathong scrolls to it
core/fallback2d includes NormalizedCylindricalCoord → 4-quadrant 2D view converter (prepared for Christmas / CNY)

stories.summary: Instanced rendering & memory cleanup audit
stories.goal: No crashes or leaks on real phones.
ac: InstancedMesh for repeated flowers, leaves and riverside trees
Zone switching on a real mobile device disposes geometry/material; memory stays flat across repeated switches
Findings documented with before/after numbers

epics.summary: Loop 9 — Visual Upgrade: Clay-toy Look & Living Riverside
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-25 (open questions 26–38): the scene looks stiff, dark and lifeless. Target look: docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png — soft clay / toy shapes, pastel colours, a wide river, a lit village, people walking along the river. Engine, coords and stored data stay as they are.

stories.summary: Art direction & LookDev v2 — match the reference image
stories.goal: One shared look (palette, materials, light) that every model and scene card builds on, so the world reads soft, warm and alive like the reference instead of stiff and dark.
ac: docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png is the visual target; an art-direction note (docs/design/loy-krathong-look.md) records the palette, material rules and light setup; every value lives in config (scene.config.ts or a look config), no inline magic numbers
Materials read as soft clay / toy: rounded (bevelled) silhouettes, matte pastel colours, no hard black shadows; soft contact or blob shadows under objects on every 3D tier (a cheap variant on LOW)

Two light presets, day and night (open question 32): by default the scene follows the real local time of the device (day / night hours in config) and a day / night switch lets the user override it; the choice is kept on the device only. In both presets land, houses and trees are clearly readable, the village is never a dark silhouette, and candle flames glow visibly at night

Applied to the existing scene without changing any stored coord or appearance data; quality tiers and reduced motion are respected and the per-tier budgets in performance.config.ts hold (r3f-perf-reviewer PASS)
Before / after screenshots at phone and desktop size are attached to the PR

stories.summary: Krathong model v2 — layered leaves, flowers, glowing candle
stories.goal: The krathong, the star of the scene, looks hand-made and charming like the reference.
ac: Every customizer option in the appearance registry (base, leaves, flowers, candle, incense) has a v2 model in the new look; appearance keys and stored appearance data are unchanged, so krathongs already saved render with the new models
Layered banana-leaf petals around a rounded base, flowers with visible petals and a centre, a candle whose flame glows and flickers gently (static under reduced motion; flicker within WCAG 2.3.1)
The same v2 models are used in the customizer preview, the pier / release ritual and the river
Repeated parts stay instanced and a full 80-item zone stays within the tier budgets; draw calls and FPS are recorded in the PR the same way as docs/perf/MFW-34.md
Geometry and materials are shared and disposed on unmount / zone switch; no per-frame allocation

stories.summary: Riverside environment v2 — wider river, rounded land, lit village
stories.goal: A bigger river in a soft, lit, lived-in riverside like the reference.
ac: The river is clearly wider and is the main feature of the view; the owner approves the width from the PR screenshots and the cap stays 80 krathongs per zone (open question 38). The lane geometry is widened in config only: stored SplinePathCoord values stay valid, the 3D ↔ 2D round-trip tests still pass, and collision spacing and the 80-item zone capacity are re-checked by tests
Land has soft rounded banks and gentle height changes; puffy rounded trees, bushes, rocks and a wooden pier as in the reference

Village: several houses with different roofs and colours; in the night preset windows and riverside lanterns are warmly lit so the village is never dark, in the day preset they are off; krathongs remain the most prominent objects
Stylized water: soft colour with gentle moving highlights / ripples near banks and krathongs (static under reduced motion; a cheap variant on LOW)
Repeated scenery uses InstancedMesh, everything is disposed on zone switch / unmount, and the tier budgets hold (r3f-perf-reviewer PASS; draw calls and FPS recorded in the PR)

stories.summary: Living world — villagers walking along the river and ambient life
stories.goal: The riverside feels alive: people stroll along the river and small things move.
ac: Small villagers — simple silhouettes are enough (owner, 2026-11-25) — walk along riverside paths and some stop to watch the river; their positions are derived deterministically from a path parameter and the clock (no physics, no stored state)
Villager count per tier comes from config (fewer on MEDIUM, fewest or none on LOW); they are instanced or share geometry and material; no per-frame allocation
Ambient life, at least two of: fireflies / floating light motes, chimney smoke, swaying trees, ducks or birds, flickering lanterns (the lead picks; values in config)
Reduced motion: villagers stand still and ambient motion is off; nothing flashes faster than WCAG 2.3.1 allows
Villagers never cover krathongs on the water and do not block taps on the river

stories.summary: 2D fallback matches the new look
stories.goal: FALLBACK_2D shows the same world, not an older-looking one.
ac: FlatRiverView and FlatKrathongPreview use the v2 palette and redrawn shapes (krathong parts, banks, houses, trees) so the 2D view reads as the same world as 3D
2D reads the same coords and appearance keys as 3D (invariant B): the wider river from 9.3 arrives through the shared lane projection, not a 2D-only number; round-trip tests stay green
FALLBACK_2D still downloads no three.js code; the FALLBACK_2D e2e flow is green; before / after screenshots are attached to the PR

epics.summary: Loop 10 — Full-screen Stage, Minimal UI & Automatic Event
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-25 (open questions 26, 28, 33): no event picker — the app shows the festival that is on now (Loy Krathong only during the private test); the world fills the whole screen; the web UI is minimal and beautiful.

stories.summary: Active event by date — remove the event selector
stories.goal: People land directly in the festival that is happening now; there is nothing to choose.
ac: Each event config declares its date window (start / end, Asia/Bangkok); a pure resolver returns the active event for a given time; unit tests cover inside, outside and boundary times
The app opens straight into the active event; the event selector, the festival list and the Coming Soon cards are removed from the user flow (supersedes open question 19)
Private-test override: one server-side config value forces the active event; it is set to Loy Krathong now, so the test shows only Loy Krathong whatever the date
When no event is active (open question 33) the app shows one calm screen with the name and dates of the festival for that time (the nearest one in the roadmap), and nothing can be created
The API uses the same resolver: creating for an event that is not active is rejected; reads keep working for the active event

stories.summary: Full-screen stage layout — the world fills the viewport, UI floats on top
stories.goal: The scene is the whole screen on phone and desktop.
ac: In every mode that shows the scene, the 3D canvas (and the 2D fallback) fills the whole viewport (100dvh × 100vw, safe-area insets respected) on phone and desktop: no page chrome, no letterboxing, no page scroll

All controls (customizer, wish, release, zone navigation, My Creations, inspect) are overlays — bottom sheets and floating buttons on phones, side panels on wide screens — and never push or shrink the canvas
The scene stays framed at any aspect ratio (camera zoom adapts; pier and river stay in view); rotating the phone or resizing the window does not reset the camera or the flow state
Overlays receive their own touches and the stage receives the rest; e2e covers 360×640, 390×844 and 1440×900
Lazy loading from 3.4 is kept: no three.js chunk is downloaded before the tier is decided, and FALLBACK_2D never downloads it

stories.summary: Minimal UI redesign — design tokens and restyle of every screen
stories.goal: A calm, minimal, beautiful interface that lets the scene be the hero.
ac: Design tokens (colour, type scale, radius, spacing, shadow, motion) are defined once (Tailwind theme / CSS variables) and documented in docs/design/ui.md; one Thai-capable web font is loaded with next/font
Every screen is restyled with the tokens: intro, customizer, wish, release, world HUD, zone navigation, My Creations, inspect popup, owner wish section, notices and the 2D fallback frame
Minimal: at most one primary action is visible per step, secondary actions sit behind icons or sheets, and overlays are light enough that the scene stays visible
Accessible: touch targets at least MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_PX, WCAG AA contrast on top of the scene, visible focus, keyboard reachable, UI transitions off under reduced motion
Behaviour is unchanged (look and layout only); all existing e2e flows are green; before / after screenshots are attached to the PR

epics.summary: Loop 11 — Explore the World: Camera Travel, Endless River & Scene Gimmicks
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-25 (open questions 30, 34, 35, 37): dragging moves the camera along the world instead of only rotating; the scene keeps rendering as you travel; things in the scene react when pressed.

stories.summary: Camera drag-to-travel — drag pans the camera, not only rotates
stories.goal: People can drag to move around the world freely.
ac: WORLD_EXPLORE: a one-finger or mouse drag moves the camera across the world, following the finger; pinch (or wheel) zooms; rotation stays available on a two-finger twist and on a button (open question 34)
The camera itself moves (the legacy scene-group pan / rotate transform is removed); lights stay world-fixed; fly-to, the highlight ring, Find My and tap picking keep working after any pan or zoom
Soft bounds keep the river in view; release has a gentle ease-out (none under reduced motion)

Tap and drag stay separated (a short tap interacts, a drag travels); CUSTOMIZE and RITUAL_RELEASE gestures are unchanged; unit tests cover the gesture mapping and the bounds, e2e covers drag-pan with touch and mouse
No per-frame allocation while dragging

stories.summary: Endless river — the scene keeps rendering as you travel
stories.goal: Drag along the river and the world keeps going: no dead end and no manual zone switch (open question 37).
ac: Travelling along the river never reaches an edge: banks, trees, houses and villagers continue ahead and behind, generated deterministically from the position along the river (everyone sees the same scenery)

Zones stream in seamlessly: the neighbouring zone's krathongs load before they come into view, far zones are unloaded and disposed, and the number of rendered items stays within the tier budget (80 per zone, invariant E); the zone navigator becomes a position indicator and jump shortcut. When the event has only one zone (or after the last zone) the river wraps around: the same zone comes back as if the river flows on (open question 37)

Positions are still derived only from stored coords (zone_id + SplinePathCoord); nothing new is persisted; the 2D fallback keeps reading the same data through the same stretch mapping as the 3D scene (unit-tested agreement); the continuous 2D river view is 11.5
Memory stays flat during a long travel and no hitch exceeds the tier budget when a zone streams in (probe numbers recorded in the PR the same way as docs/perf/MFW-34.md)
Find My and fly-to work along the whole river; reduced motion uses instant cuts

stories.summary: Bug: nothing in the scene reacts to taps
stories.goal: Owner report 2026-11-25: on the deployed app nothing in the scene can be pressed. Taps must work and be easy to discover.
ac: Reproduce on the production build on a phone and on a desktop browser and record the cause in the PR (which taps fail — water, lamp, krathong — in which mode and with which pointer type)

In WORLD_EXPLORE a short tap or click on water makes a ripple, on a lamp lights it, and on a krathong opens the inspect popup — with touch and mouse, on every 3D tier; the krathong tap also works in FALLBACK_2D
Tap targets are at least MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_PX on screen (invisible hit proxies where the model is smaller, e.g. lamps)
A first-visit hint shows that the scene can be tapped; it goes away after the first tap and is static under reduced motion
An e2e test taps water, a lamp and a krathong on the production build and asserts each reaction

stories.summary: More scene gimmicks — houses, trees, villagers and sky lanterns react to taps
stories.goal: Small delights everywhere: most things in the scene answer a tap.
ac: New tap reactions (open question 35): house → windows light up; tree → leaves shake; villager → hops; lantern → a sky lantern (โคมลอย) rises and fades; sky → a firework is launched (the chimney smoke, the falling leaves and the villager wave are 11.6)

Anything in the scene can be interacted with (owner, 2026-11-25): every visible object type answers a tap; feedback is natural (a small bounce or light change, no rings or halos — see 13.3) so people learn what can be tapped
Every effect comes from ObjectPoolManager with a fixed cap from config: no new objects per tap and no per-frame allocation (r3f-perf-reviewer PASS)
Reduced motion: reactions are instant state changes without bounce or particles; nothing flashes faster than WCAG 2.3.1 allows
Unit tests cover each reaction's timing and pool cap; e2e taps at least one new gimmick

stories.summary: Remove the 2D fallback
stories.goal: The owner decided on 2026-11-26 to drop the flat 2D fallback ("เอา 2d ออกไปเลย"); this replaces the earlier 11.5 (continuous 2D river), which is no longer built. Only the 3D scene remains, with the quality tiers HIGH, MEDIUM and LOW.
ac: The FALLBACK_2D tier is gone: the tiers are HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW in useDeviceStore and performance.config.ts; a device whose FPS stays low steps down to LOW and stays there instead of switching to 2D

Without WebGL the stage shows a short Thai notice that the device cannot show the 3D scene, instead of the scene; nothing crashes, and an e2e covers it (the notice text and what else the page offers are a loop decision recorded for the owner)

src/core/fallback2d, src/components/canvas2d, the 2D-only tests and e2e specs, the 2D day/night switch path and every import of them are removed; shared code used by 3D (coordinate converters, stretch mapping, zone paging) stays, with its 3D round-trip tests

Invariant A (parametric coordinates only) is unchanged; CLAUDE.md invariants B and F, docs/spec/open-questions.md and the look doc record the owner decision; no shader program or render budget is added
typecheck, lint, unit tests, build and the full e2e are green

stories.summary: Scene gimmicks, part 2 — chimney smoke, falling leaves and a villager wave
stories.goal: The rest of the tap reactions the owner asked for (open question 35), split from 11.4 by the lead on 2026-11-26 because 11.4 was too large for one PR.
ac: House tap: besides the window light-up of 11.4, a puff of smoke rises from the roof (or from a small chimney added to the house model) and fades
Tree tap: besides the leaf shake of 11.4, a few leaves fall and fade on the ground
Villager tap: the villager waves (or keeps the hop of 11.4 if a wave needs arms the silhouette does not have — the lead decides and records it)
Every effect comes from ObjectPoolManager with a fixed cap from config; no new shader program, no new objects per tap, no per-frame allocation; natural look, no rings or halos (13.3)
Reduced motion: instant state changes without particles; unit tests cover each reaction's timing and pool cap; e2e taps at least one of the new reactions

epics.summary: Loop 12 — Wish Visibility Switch & Display Name
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-25 (open questions 29, 36): the wish is private by default and its owner can switch it open or closed; when open, everyone sees both the name and the wish. Replaces the one-time private / anonymous-public choice of spec §6.4 Task 4.3.

stories.summary: Wish visibility switch & display name — data and API
stories.goal: The server lets an owner open or close a wish at any time without ever leaking a closed one.
ac: New migration file (existing migrations untouched): a nullable public display_name on creations_public and an encrypted private display name next to the private wish; RLS and grants stay closed (anon and authenticated denied on every table, view and function)

POST /api/creations accepts an optional displayName (open question 36); the name passes the same server moderation guard as public wish text (PII and profanity, Thai and English) and a length limit from config (placeholder value)

A new ownership endpoint (POST; raw owner token only in the body; constant-time hash compare; uniform not-found answer) switches a creation open or closed. Opening: the server decrypts the wish and name, runs the moderation guard, and only if it passes writes public_wish_text and display_name and clears the ciphertext. Closing: encrypts both back into the private table and clears them from the public row
The text and name exist in exactly one store at a time; a wish hidden by reports or moderation stays hidden and cannot be opened again (open question 36)
Public responses carry display_name and public_wish_text only for open, visible wishes; a test asserts owner_token, owner_token_hash and private_wish_text never appear
Works with the in-memory repository when Supabase env is absent; tests cover open → close → open, a moderation rejection on open, and a wrong token

stories.summary: Wish visibility switch & display name — UI
stories.goal: Writing a wish is simple: a name, the wish, and one switch that says who can see it.
ac: Wish step: an optional name field and a single switch "เปิดให้ทุกคนเห็น" (off = private, the default) replace the two-option choice; the helper text says clearly that when it is on, everyone sees the name and the wish; an empty name is shown as "ไม่ระบุชื่อ" (open question 36)

The owner can flip the switch later from My Creations / the owner section of the inspect popup on the owning device; the change shows at once and survives a reload; a moderation rejection shows the reasons and the wish stays private
Inspect popup: an open wish shows name + wish + Report; a closed wish shows only the krathong to everyone else (no name, no text)
The raw token is sent only in the POST body; the name and wish are not kept on the device outside the existing owner flow; the 2D fallback has the same switch and popup
Component tests cover the switch states and errors; e2e covers create-open, switch to private and switch back

epics.summary: Loop 13 — Generated 3D Models, Natural Look & Bigger Scene
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-25 (second review): the procedural models still look flat. Use generated 3D models (Higgsfield image/text-to-3D → GLB) made from docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png for the krathong, houses, lamps and fireworks; people can be simple silhouettes. No yellow rings around objects — the scene should look natural; anything in the scene can be interacted with; the scene should fill the screen (it looks small).

stories.summary: Generated-model pipeline (GLB) and krathong model from the reference
stories.goal: A repeatable way to bring generated 3D models into the scene within the mobile budget, proven on the krathong.
ac: Krathong part models are generated with Higgsfield (image/text-to-3D) from docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png, exported as GLB, and optimised offline (decimated, compressed, textures ≤ the tier's max texture size); source prompts / job ids and the optimise steps are documented in docs/design/models.md so a model can be regenerated

A loader module loads GLB assets lazily after the tier is decided (never in the first-screen bundle, never on FALLBACK_2D), shares geometry / material / texture across instances and disposes them on unmount and zone switch

Every customizer option still maps to a model (appearance keys and stored data unchanged); river krathongs stay instanced; a full 80-item zone stays inside the tier budgets (draw calls, triangles and programs recorded like docs/perf/MFW-34.md)
LOW uses a lighter variant (fewer triangles / smaller textures) or keeps the procedural model; the choice is in performance.config.ts
Asset files are committed under public/ with a size budget enforced by a test; licences / generation terms are noted in docs/design/models.md

stories.summary: Generated models for houses, lamps and fireworks; silhouette villagers
stories.goal: The riverside props look as rich as the reference instead of flat boxes.
ac: Houses and riverside lamps use generated GLB models (13.1 pipeline) placed by the existing layout; repeated props are instanced; windows / lamp heads still light up in the night preset

Fireworks: a pooled burst effect (ObjectPoolManager, fixed cap) with a generated or stylised model / sprite, launched by the sky tap of 11.4; flashes stay within WCAG 2.3.1 and are static under reduced motion
Villagers are simple dark silhouettes (owner: "คนอาจจะแค่เป็นเงาๆก็พอ") walking the riverside paths of 9.4; no faces or detail
Tier budgets hold on HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW with before / after numbers; everything is disposed on zone switch; r3f-perf-reviewer PASS
Before / after screenshots at phone and desktop size, day and night, are attached to the PR

stories.summary: Natural look — remove the yellow rings and halos around objects
stories.goal: Nothing in the scene is circled or haloed; light looks natural.
ac: The yellow discs / rings drawn around krathongs, lamps and selected objects (flame glow pool, lamp light pools on the ground, highlight ring) are removed or replaced by natural lighting: a small soft flame glow on the candle itself and warm light that falls off smoothly without a visible ring edge

Selection / Find My feedback no longer uses a ring: the object gets a gentle natural cue (a brief bounce, a slightly brighter flame or a soft rim) that still follows a moving krathong and is still perceivable under reduced motion and for colour-blind users
Day and night presets both look natural in screenshots (no hard-edged yellow circle anywhere); krathongs are still easy to spot at night
Existing behaviour is kept: Find My still brings the krathong into view and marks it; e2e and unit tests updated only where they asserted the ring
No new shader program and no per-frame allocation; r3f-perf-reviewer PASS

stories.summary: Bigger scene — the world fills the screen
stories.goal: The scene no longer looks small inside the screen; land and river reach every edge.
ac: The default framing is closer: the krathong, pier and village read clearly larger on phone and desktop (framed world size and zoom cap in config; owner approves from screenshots)
No empty background shows at any viewport size or after any pan / rotate / zoom within the bounds: ground, river and scenery extend past every screen edge
The pier and both banks are still reachable by panning; the release ritual drop mapping and tap targets (≥ MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_PX at 360 px wide) still work
e2e covers 360×640, 390×844 and 1440×900: no background pixel at the four corners and the centre; existing framing tests updated to the new numbers
Tier budgets hold (the closer view must not raise fill-rate past the pixel caps)

stories.summary: Detailed krathong leaves and flowers (no more boxes and triangles)
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-25): the models are only squares and triangles — leaves and flowers need real detail, like the reference.
ac: Banana-leaf petals are real leaf shapes: a curved, tapered blade with a midrib crease, bent outward and slightly cupped, overlapping in layers like docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png — no flat triangles or diamonds

Flowers are real blooms: several rounded, cupped petals in one or two rings around a raised centre, with small per-petal variation; each flower type in the registry (marigold, orchid, lotus) is recognisably different

The base, candle and flame get matching detail (rounded lip, wax drip or wick, soft teardrop flame); appearance keys and stored data are unchanged, so saved krathongs render with the new models; the customizer, pier and river use the same models

Detail is tiered: full detail for the own krathong (customizer / pier) and on HIGH; lighter variants for river krathongs on MEDIUM and LOW so a full 80-item zone stays inside the tier budgets (triangles, draw calls and programs recorded like docs/perf/MFW-34.md; no new shader program)
Geometry is shared, instanced on the river and disposed on unmount / zone switch; no per-frame allocation; before / after close-up screenshots (day and night) are attached to the PR

stories.summary: Detailed foliage — leafy trees, bushes and riverside plants
stories.goal: Trees and bushes read as foliage instead of blobs and cones.
ac: Tree canopies are built from clustered leaf clumps (several overlapping rounded masses with a broken silhouette) on a tapered, slightly bent trunk with a branch or two, in the clay look of docs/spec/assets/loy-krathong-look-ref.png; at least two tree shapes
Bushes and riverside plants (reeds, lotus pads or grass tufts along the bank) add detail at the water edge; nothing covers the krathong lane or the walking paths
Repeated foliage is instanced; the environment stays inside ENVIRONMENT_RENDER_BUDGETS per tier (LOW uses the lighter variant) with before / after numbers; no new shader program
Gentle sway on HIGH / MEDIUM only where the scene is already animating; static under reduced motion
Before / after screenshots at phone and desktop size, day and night, are attached to the PR

epics.summary: Loop 14 — Owner Review 3: Minimal Krathong UI & Scene Polish
epics.description: Owner request 2026-11-26 (third review, with a screenshot of the world view): make the UI minimal — a Find My button that opens a compact krathong picker with short dates, a fading speech bubble over another person's krathong instead of a text panel, a day/night toggle shown as a coloured sun / moon symbol, and the camera-rotate button at the top left; and polish the scene — a fuller village, a lamp tap that simply turns the lamp on, a tap on empty ground that randomly launches a firework or a sky lantern, a second flower type on the krathong so it looks full, and water waves with more depth.

stories.summary: Minimal HUD — krathong picker, day/night toggle, camera button top left
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): the UI shows less text and fewer panels; the scene and the krathongs carry the experience. Split by the loop lead on 2026-11-26: the fading wish bubble is 14.6.
ac: Find My is one round icon button; tapping it opens a compact picker of the user's own krathongs (small krathong thumbnail plus a short date such as "26 NOV 2026" and the time — no weekday names such as MON / TUE, no explanatory text); choosing one brings that krathong into view (reduced motion: instant cut) and closes the picker; with one krathong the button goes straight to it (the picker layout and the one-krathong shortcut are loop decisions recorded for the owner)

The day / night control is one toggle button showing a coloured sun or moon symbol and no text; tapping it switches DAY ↔ NIGHT; until the user touches it the scene keeps following the real time of day (owner decision, open question 32); how the user returns to the real-time default is a loop decision recorded for the owner; the button has an accessible Thai label
The camera-rotate button moves to the top left with the other round buttons; behaviour unchanged; every button keeps MIN_TOUCH_TARGET_PX and does not cover the river at 390×844, 360×640 and 1440×900
e2e covers the picker (choose a krathong → it comes into view), the toggle (DAY ↔ NIGHT) and the rotate button position; before / after screenshots at phone and desktop sizes, DAY and NIGHT

stories.summary: Lamp lights up; empty-ground tap launches a firework or a sky lantern at random
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): every tap feels natural — a lamp tap simply turns the lamp on, and the sky tap is a surprise. Split by the loop lead on 2026-11-26 from the larger scene-polish card (fuller village 14.3, second flower type 14.4, deeper water 14.5).
ac: Tapping a lamp turns its light on (the lamp head glows; any warm light on the ground must not read as a ring, halo or disc) and nothing rises from it — no sky lantern from a lamp; reduced motion: the light switches on instantly

Tapping empty ground / bank launches either a firework or a sky lantern at random (both pooled with fixed caps; the generator is seeded so tests are deterministic; the split is DRAFT); unit tests and e2e cover the lamp and the random sky tap; no new shader program on LOW; before / after screenshots DAY and NIGHT

stories.summary: Fuller village along both banks
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): the village should fill the scene (split from 14.2).
ac: More houses and matching props along both banks so the scene looks full at the default framing on phone and desktop, DAY and NIGHT; scenery repeats per stretch as in 11.2; repeated parts stay instanced; per-tier render budgets kept (any raise stated openly) and the environment budget test covers the new props; before / after screenshots

stories.summary: Second flower type on the krathong, chosen in the customizer
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): the bare areas of the krathong base should look full, with a choice of two flower types (split from 14.2).
ac: The krathong model gets a second flower type that fills the bare areas of the base, and the customizer lets the user choose between the two flower types; the server-side appearance parser accepts the new key
Krathongs saved before this card render exactly as before (fixture test); unit tests and e2e cover the flower choice; before / after screenshots DAY and NIGHT

stories.summary: Water with more depth
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): the river waves should look more three-dimensional (split from 14.2).
ac: The river water shows more depth (gentle wave shading and highlights that move with the flow) within the per-tier budgets and without a new shader program on LOW (E2E_MAX_SHADER_PROGRAMS); reduced motion keeps the water still; before / after screenshots DAY and NIGHT

stories.summary: Fading wish bubble over another person's krathong
stories.goal: Owner (2026-11-26): tapping someone else's krathong shows only a short-lived speech bubble, no text panel (split from 14.1).
ac: Tapping another person's krathong shows only a speech bubble with its public wish text floating above that krathong in the scene, following it as it drifts, and fading out after a few seconds (duration DRAFT); the old text panel is removed; private wish text never appears (invariant C); the bubble position is derived from the stored coord (invariant A)
e2e covers the bubble (appears over the tapped krathong, follows it, fades, no panel); before / after screenshots at phone size, DAY and NIGHT
